title.narrative: Scaling up Emergency Health Support Services in Ed Daein, East Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtSudan crisis, which commenced on April 15, 2023, has led to significant humanitarian challenges within the country and the wider region. The conflict has resulted in the displacement of millions of people, causing disruption to trade, market functionality, household mobility, humanitarian assistance, and basic service provision Nearly 26 million Sudanese-half the entire country-are facing high levels of acute food insecurity. Nearly 11 million people have been forced to flee their homes or have left Sudan altogether. Over 70% of Sudan’s health care system has collapsed and preventable disease outbreaks are becoming common. ltbrgt ltbrgtIn response to this crisis, the project aims to provide life-saving interventions, focusing on the most affected locationsstates in East Darfur region. The primary objective is to deliver life-saving health services to those in need, with a particular focus on displaced people and vulnerable host communities. Under health, the project target 150,000 direct beneficiaries while for nutrition 36,437 direct beneficiaries are targeted. The project will upgrade four clinics to operate 24/7, ensuring continuous access to essential services including outpatient consultations for both communicable and non-communicable diseases, trauma and wound care, reproductive health services including antenatal care, safe delivery with qualified personnel, post-natal care, family planning, access to referral and supporting GBV survivors to access medical care. For nutrition the package will include identifying malnourished cases through routine and mass MUAC screening, admitting and managing identified cases through Outpatient therapeutic program (OTP), Targeted Supplementary feeding Program (TSFP) and also promotion, support and protection of IYCN practices. Two new Stabilization Centers will be established in Ad Daein town and Yassin Locality to manage SAM cases with complications, reducing mortality rates among severely malnourished children.Thenbspproject will also expand maternal and neonatal care services at the Elneem PHC EmONC Centre, helping to prevent maternal and neonatal deaths. The rehabilitation of damaged health service points, including EPI and MHPSS units, will ensure the continuity of essential public health services. ltbrgtThese activities align with the Health and Nutrition Clusters' Strategic Response Plans, focusing on restoring essential healthcare in conflict-affected areas. By expanding services for vulnerable populations, the project aims to stabilize and improve health outcomes in Ad Daein and nearby areas, directly addressing the critical needs. ltbrgtThe target groups include internally displaced persons (IDPs), host communities, and vulnerable populations like pregnant women, newborns, and those suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in Ad Daein, East Darfur. The recent closure of the Ad Daein Teaching Hospital has left these groups without access to critical healthcare services, resulting in significant gaps in emergency care, maternal and child health, and SAM treatment. ltbrgtExisting healthcare capacity is overstretched, with remaining clinics already at full capacity before the hospital's closure. The healthcare workforce, while committed, is insufficient to handle the increased demand, and critical shortages of medical supplies and equipment further limit service delivery. ltbrgtThe success of the projectnbspwill hinge on close coordination among consortium members, the health cluster, and other stakeholders. Collaboration with organizations such as WHO, UNICEF, WFP, and the FMOH for the provision of essential supplies, is also anticipated. Alight will strive to make the targeted individuals aware of the available service packages in the language primarily used by the beneficiaries. Complaints and feedback mechanism will be established through a complaint desk, hotlines where feasible, and other channels, with the collected feedback being analyzed to enhance services.nbspltbrgtlt/pgt
